title: Diary Entry About First Day at School: 6 Examples
description: Diary entry about first day at school: 6 model examples for kids and exam students, the correct format, useful phrases, and a free page to write your own.
h1: Diary entry about first day at school (6 examples)
intro: A diary entry about your first day at school starts with the date and day, opens with **Dear Diary**, tells what happened in the past tense, says how you felt, and ends with a closing and your name. Below are 6 complete model entries, from a short one for young kids to longer ones for class 9 and 10, plus phrases, steps and a page to write your own.

writer.title: Dear diary,
writer.hint: Today was my first day at school. I felt...

sections.h2: Diary entry format for your first day at school

blocks.p: Every diary entry follows the same simple pattern. Teachers and examiners look for these parts, so put all of them in, even in a short answer. See the full [diary entry format](/diary-entry-format/) guide if you want more detail.

ul: **Date, day and time** at the top left, for example: 16 June 2025, Monday, 9:30 p.m.
**Dear Diary,** as the greeting on its own line.
**The body** in the first person (I, me, we) and the past tense (I walked, I felt, we laughed).
**Feelings** before, during and after the day. This is what makes it a diary and not a report.
**A closing** such as Good night, See you tomorrow or Love, and then **your name**.

blocks.tip: Many school and exam questions ask for about 100 to 150 words. Always check the word limit in the question and stay close to it.

sections.h2: Short diary entry about first day at school (for kids)

blocks.p: This one is about 80 words. It suits grades 2 to 5, or anyone who needs a quick, simple model.

example.label: About 80 words
example.title: Dear Diary,
example.text:
Today was my first day at Oakfield Primary.
I was so nervous that my tummy hurt at breakfast.
My teacher, Mrs. Hall, has a big smile and a pet fish
called Bubbles in our classroom.
A girl named Ruby sat next to me. She lent me her pink
pencil, and we played tag at break time.
By lunchtime I was not scared anymore.
I think I am going to like it here.
See you tomorrow,
Maisie

blocks.p: Notice how it uses short sentences, one or two details (the fish, the pink pencil) and a clear change in feeling from nervous to happy. That change is the heart of a good first day entry.

sections.h2: Diary entry about first day at new school in 120 to 150 words

blocks.p: This is the length most often asked for in class 6 to 10 English exams. It has every part of the format and a clear beginning, middle and end.

example.label: Exam style, about 140 words
example.title: Dear Diary,
example.text:
Today was my first day at Green Valley School, and I was
both excited and nervous. We moved to Pune only last week,
so I did not know a single person in my new class.
When I walked into Class 9B, everyone turned to look at me.
My cheeks went hot. Our class teacher, Mrs. Kulkarni, asked
me to introduce myself. My voice shook, but I managed it.
At lunch, a boy named Ishaan waved me over to his table.
He showed me the library, the science labs and the best
spot on the field for cricket. By the last bell, we were
laughing like old friends.
I came home tired but relieved. I still miss my old school,
but today showed me that a new place can feel like home.
I cannot wait for tomorrow.
Good night,
Rohan

blocks.p: Why this scores well: the date and time are complete, the events go in order, there is one real moment of feeling (hot cheeks, shaking voice), and the ending looks ahead. It also stays inside the word limit.

sections.h2: Longer diary entries about the first day of school

blocks.p: These longer models are good for creative writing tasks, class 8 to 10 practice, or when you just want ideas. Each one tells a different kind of first day.

example.label: About 170 words
example.title: Dear Diary,
example.text:
I am finally a high school learner! I woke up at five
because I was too excited to sleep. Mama ironed my new
blazer twice and took about twenty photos at the gate.
The school is huge. I got lost three times looking for
Room 14 and walked into a Grade 11 science class by mistake.
Everyone laughed, but a kind girl named Zanele walked me
to the right room. It turns out she is in my class too.
Maths was hard, and the teacher talks very fast. Life
Orientation was fun because we played a name game. I now
know that Sipho can do a backflip and Kayla has four cats.
The worst part was break. I did not know where to stand,
so I pretended to read my timetable for ten minutes.
Then Zanele found me again and shared her vetkoek.
Tonight my legs are sore from all the stairs, but my heart
feels light. Tomorrow I am going to draw a map of the school!
Love,
Thandi

blocks.h3: First day at school in a new country

example.label: About 165 words
example.title: Dear Diary,
example.text:
Today was my first day at Lincoln Middle School. Two months
ago I lived in Bogotá. Now I live in Ohio, and everything
is in English, even the lunch menu.
In homeroom I understood only half of what Mr. Carter said.
I smiled and nodded a lot. When he called my name, he said
it perfectly, and that made me feel welcome right away.
The hardest part was lunch. The cafeteria was loud, and I
did not know where to sit. A boy named Jayden asked if I
liked soccer. I said yes, and he moved his tray so I could
sit down. We talked about our favorite players with our
hands and a few words, and somehow it worked.
In art class we painted something that reminds us of home.
I painted the mountains. My teacher said it was beautiful.
I am tired from thinking in English all day, but I am proud
of myself. Tomorrow I will learn five new words.
Hasta mañana,
Mateo

blocks.h3: A funny first day at secondary school

example.label: About 150 words
example.title: Dear Diary,
example.text:
You will not believe what I did on my first day at
secondary school. I sat in the wrong lesson for an hour.
My timetable said S2, so I went to the second floor and
found a door marked S2. I sat at the back and got out my
pencil case. The teacher started talking about castles.
I thought, strange, I have Science now. But I was too shy
to say anything.
At the end, she checked her register and asked who I was.
It turns out S2 means Science Block, Room 2. The whole class
laughed, and after a minute, so did I.
My real Science teacher, Mr. Okoro, just grinned and said,
"At least you learned some history." I now have two lessons
of notes and a story nobody in Year 7 will forget.
Lesson learned: read the key at the bottom of the timetable.
Cheers,
Kabir

blocks.h3: First day at school as a new teacher

blocks.p: Some exam questions ask you to write as a teacher. The format stays the same.

example.label: About 145 words
example.title: Dear Diary,
example.text:
Today was my first day as a real teacher. I taught as a
trainee before, but this time the class is mine.
Twenty-eight Grade 4 faces looked up at me at 8 a.m., and
my hands were shaking more than theirs.
I started with a game where everyone said their name and
a favorite food. A shy boy named Liam whispered "chips" so
softly I had to lean in. By home time he was helping me
hand out books.
Not everything went well. The projector would not work,
and I ran out of time in the reading lesson. But when the
bell rang, a girl named Aisha hugged me and said, "See you
tomorrow, Miss." I almost cried in the car park.
I am exhausted, and I have a lot to learn. But I know now
that I chose the right job.
Good night,
Grace

sections.h2: Useful words and phrases for a first day at school diary entry

ul: Before: nervous, anxious, jittery, excited, curious, worried, shy
During: overwhelmed, lost, awkward, surprised, welcome, amazed
After: relieved, proud, happy, tired but happy, hopeful, homesick
uniform, school bag, timetable, assembly, register, homeroom
classmates, class teacher, principal, head teacher, seat partner
corridors, staff room, library, labs, playground, canteen, cafeteria
break time, recess, lunch hour, last bell, home time
I could hardly sleep last night because I was so excited.
My heart was racing as I walked through the school gate.
Everything felt new and a little strange.
I had butterflies in my stomach when the teacher called my name.
A friendly classmate offered to show me around.
By lunchtime, most of my worries had melted away.
I was nervous at first, but the day turned out better than I expected.
I cannot wait to go back tomorrow.

blocks.p: Use two or three of these, not all of them. A real detail from your own day (a smell, a name, a funny mistake) always beats a stock phrase. For more topics to practice with, see our list of [diary entry topics](/diary-entry-topics/).

sections.h2: How to write your own first day at school diary entry

steps.name: Write the date, day and time
steps.text: Put them at the top. Writing the time (evening is common) shows you are writing at the end of the day.

steps.name: Start with Dear Diary
steps.text: Then write one opening line that says what today was: "Today was my first day at..."

steps.name: Say how you felt before school
steps.text: Were you excited, scared, or both? One or two sentences is enough.

steps.name: Tell the main events in order
steps.text: Arriving, meeting your teacher, a classmate, lunch or break, one lesson. Pick two or three moments, not everything.

steps.name: Add one detail and one feeling to each moment
steps.text: "My hands were shaking" or "she shared her snack" brings the page to life.

steps.name: End with a thought and a closing
steps.text: What did you learn, or what are you looking forward to? Then a closing like Good night and your name.

ul: **Forgetting the date or the name.** These are easy marks. Do not lose them.
**Writing in the present tense.** Diary entries look back on the day, so write I went, not I go.
**Writing in the third person.** It is your diary. Use I, not he or she.
**Listing events with no feelings.** "I went to class. I had lunch. I came home." reads like a timetable. Say how each part felt.
**Ending like a letter.** Do not write Yours faithfully or Yours sincerely. A diary closing is warm and simple.
**Going far over the word limit.** In an exam, a tidy 130 words beats a messy 300.

blocks.p: Younger writers can find more help in our guide to keeping a [diary for kids](/diary-for-kids/) and in these [journal prompts for kids](/journal-prompts-for-kids/). For more model answers on other topics, browse our [diary entry examples](/diary-entry-examples/).

faq.q: How do you start a diary entry about your first day at school?
faq.a: Write the date, day and time at the top, then Dear Diary on the next line. Your first sentence should say what the entry is about, for example: Today was my first day at my new school, and I could hardly sleep last night because I was so nervous. Starting with a feeling pulls the reader in straight away.

faq.q: How many words should a diary entry about first day at school be?
faq.a: Follow the word limit in your question. Most class 6 to 10 exam questions ask for 100 to 150 words. Younger children can write 60 to 100 words. For creative writing homework without a limit, 200 to 300 words gives you room for details and feelings without dragging on.

faq.q: What tense is a diary entry written in?
faq.a: Mostly the simple past tense, because you are writing about things that already happened today: I walked, I met, I felt. You can use the present tense for how you feel right now as you write, such as I am tired but happy, and the future for plans, such as I will draw a map tomorrow.

faq.q: Can I write about feeling scared or sad on my first day?
faq.a: Yes. Honest feelings make a diary entry stronger. Many good first day entries start with fear or loneliness and show a small change by the end, like a classmate sharing a snack. If the whole day was hard, it is fine to say so and end with one hope for tomorrow.

faq.q: Should a diary entry have a title?
faq.a: Usually no. A diary entry needs the date, the greeting Dear Diary, the body, a closing and your name. Some teachers ask for a heading like My First Day at School above the entry, so check your teacher's instructions or the exam pattern for your board.
